passages.provision_quote: The supreme court has mandatory and exclusive jurisdiction over any appeal from a final judgment or any other appealable order holding the apportionment unconstitutional or otherwise invalid, either in whole or in part.
passages.note: As author, Smaltz's HB 1032 has the General Assembly establish new congressional districts directly (Sec. 7) while Sec. 3 preserves Supreme Court review of apportionment challenges, matching rung 4.
passages.actor_quote: Smaltz December 1, 2025, read first time and referred to Committee on Elections and Apportionment.

passages.note: IGA bill page credits Smaltz as author; shows the House-passed bill was later defeated on Senate third reading.
Smaltz voted Yea on House final passage of the single-subject redistricting bill he authored.

rows.reasoning: Smaltz authored and voted Yea on HB 1032 (2026), a single-subject redistricting bill that has the General Assembly establish new congressional districts directly (Sec. 7) while Sec. 3 preserves the Indiana Supreme Court's mandatory and exclusive jurisdiction to hear appeals holding the apportionment unconstitutional or otherwise invalid, matching rung 4's 'state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias' rather than rung 5, whose 'without outside interference' clause fails because court review is expressly preserved.
